EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
The most critical development of the past 24 hours is the stated temporary halt of a planned US military strike against Iran, requested by Saudi Arabia, Qatar, and the UAE to allow for ongoing "serious discussions" aimed at preventing Iran from acquiring nuclear weapons. This pause occurs amidst heightened military readiness and conflicting reports on the progress of negotiations, with both sides maintaining maximalist positions and threatening further escalation. Simultaneously, Israel's northern border remains highly active with extensive IDF strikes against Hezbollah in Lebanon, and the Israeli Navy intercepted a large aid flotilla attempting to reach Gaza.

IRAN
Iran's President Pezeshkian reaffirmed the nation's resolve, stating that dialogue does not mean surrender and Iran will not back down from its legal rights. Mohsen Rezaei, senior advisor to the Leader, and Major General Abdollahi, commander of Khatam al-Anbiya, issued strong warnings that Iran's armed forces are more prepared than ever and will respond with overwhelming force to any aggression, asserting that a significant portion of Iran's military capabilities remains unused. Air defense systems were activated in Isfahan and on Qeshm Island in the Persian Gulf, with Iranian state media (Tasnim) reporting these activations were in response to "enemy drones," specifically mentioning US and Israeli unmanned aircraft over Qeshm.

Regarding negotiations with the US, an Iranian source close to the negotiating team, cited by Tasnim, stated that Iran submitted a revised 14-point proposal to the US via Pakistan. This proposal reportedly demands a permanent end to the war, the lifting of all sanctions, the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, and the release of all frozen Iranian funds, with the nuclear program to be discussed in later stages. The source also claimed the US agreed to temporarily ease oil sanctions, but Iran insists on the permanent lifting of all sanctions. Iran announced visa-free travel for Lebanese citizens for up to 15 days, effective May 22.

Economically, there are reports of gasoline rationing and queues, exacerbating public frustration. Satellite images cited by Bloomberg show approximately 23 oil tankers near Kharg Island, the largest gathering since the US blockade began. The Persian Gulf Strait Authority (PGSA) launched an official X account to provide real-time updates on Strait of Hormuz operations, emphasizing that ships require Iran's approval for passage. Internally, Nobel Peace laureate Narges Mohammadi was released from hospital in Tehran to continue recovery at home after her health deteriorated in prison. Amnesty International, cited by Vahid Online, reported that Iran executed 2,159 people in 2025, an unprecedented number.

ISRAEL
Israeli military operations were focused on Gaza and Lebanon. In Gaza, the IDF killed a Hamas sniper in the southern Strip who was planning an immediate attack. Off the coast, the Israeli Navy intercepted the "Global Sumud Flotilla," comprising approximately 57 vessels that departed from Turkey, which was attempting to challenge the naval blockade of Gaza. Six Irish citizens were among the activists arrested, and Israeli officials stated no humanitarian aid was found on the boats.

On the home front, the IDF Home Front Command updated its mobile application to improve user experience with clearer, color-coded, and audibly distinct alerts for different threat levels and an "all-clear" notification. Significant civilian incidents included a severe traffic accident on Dizengoff Street in Tel Aviv, leaving 11 injured, including a 15-year-old girl in critical condition. Another shooting incident occurred in Jadida-Makr, injuring the local council head and his deputy, marking the second such event in 24 hours in the community. Police in the US reported at least five fatalities in a shooting at an Islamic Center in San Diego, California, near a school teaching Hebrew, with two juvenile attackers among the dead.

Politically, the International Criminal Court's Office of the Prosecutor in The Hague reportedly submitted a request for an international arrest warrant against Israeli Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich in early April, citing crimes against humanity, war crimes, and apartheid. Further requests against ministers Itamar Ben Gvir, Israel Katz, and Chief of Staff Eyal Zamir are reportedly under consideration. Prime Minister Netanyahu's court appearance was canceled for "security and political reasons." Justice Minister Yariv Levin accused the Attorney General, Gali Baharav-Miara, of "political actions" concerning the case of General Roman Gofman, whose classified affidavit was released by the AG after declassification by the military. Discussions continue regarding a new draft law, with Gadi Eisenkot stating he would not compromise on the issue, even at the cost of new elections. Military and police exercises are planned for Eilat and the Western Galilee.

GAZA & WEST BANK
In the Gaza Strip, the IDF successfully eliminated a Hamas sniper in the south who was deemed an immediate threat to ground troops. The "Global Sumud Flotilla" from Turkey, consisting of approximately 57 vessels, was intercepted by the Israeli Navy while attempting to breach the naval blockade of Gaza. No humanitarian aid was found on the boats. Hamas condemned an Israeli decision to expropriate residential buildings near the Al-Aqsa Mosque in Jerusalem's Old City, calling it an "existential threat" to Palestinians. Israeli settlers were reported to have set fire to Palestinian farmland in Al-Mughayyir, northeast of Ramallah. Following the death of Azz al-Din al-Hadad, Hamas reportedly appointed Mohammed Odeh, head of military intelligence, as the new commander of its military wing.

LEBANON
The situation along the Israel-Lebanon border remains highly volatile. The IDF conducted extensive strikes, hitting over 30 Hezbollah targets across southern Lebanon, including weapon depots, surveillance posts, and military buildings. Additionally, the IDF announced a precise strike in the Beqaa Valley, near Baalbek, that killed Wael Mahmoud Abd al-Halim, the commander of Palestinian Islamic Jihad in the Beqaa region, who was reportedly coordinating operations with Hezbollah. Lebanese media indicated Halim's 17-year-old daughter was also killed. Hezbollah responded by launching rockets towards Kiryat Shmona and nearby border communities; some were intercepted, and others fell in open areas without causing injuries. An explosive drone launched by Hezbollah struck Israeli territory near the Shomera community, causing fragments to be found. The IDF also intercepted three suspected Hezbollah drones over southern Lebanon. Artillery fire and explosions were reported in the central Galilee, Ramim ridge, and Hula Valley due to IDF activity. IDF Arabic spokesperson issued evacuation warnings for three villages in southern Lebanon. Hezbollah claimed targeting an Israeli Merkava tank and a Hummer with guided missiles and attack drones in southern Lebanon.

SYRIA & IRAQ
In Iraq, drone strikes targeted the headquarters of the Komala terrorist group in Sulaymaniyah province, reportedly injuring two individuals, and also PJAK targets in the same province. The IRGC announced it foiled a large-scale weapons smuggling operation from terrorist groups based in northern Iraq, near the Kurdistan border, into Iran. Iraq's Foreign Ministry reaffirmed its policy against allowing its territory to be used for attacks on neighboring countries, following reports of three drones targeting Saudi Arabia from Iraqi airspace. The Ministry also called for cooperation and information exchange with Saudi Arabia on the matter. Kuwaiti drones were reported to have repeatedly violated Iraqi airspace over Basra in February. Separately, Iraq reportedly provided Lebanon with $2 billion worth of oil to avert a complete power blackout. In Syria, clashes broke out between IDF forces and armed individuals in the Yarmouk Basin area of Daraa province. The Syrian Foreign Minister expressed gratitude to the European Union for lifting sanctions on several Syrian government entities, including the Interior and Defense Ministries.

GULF STATES
Saudi Arabia, Qatar, and the United Arab Emirates reportedly requested that US President Trump delay his planned military strike against Iran, citing ongoing "serious discussions" for a potential agreement. The UAE confirmed that power supply was restored to Unit 3 of the Barakah nuclear power plant after a drone attack yesterday. Pakistan has deployed 8,000 troops, JF-17 fighter jets, drones, and HQ-9 air defense systems to Saudi Arabia as part of a defense pact, with Reuters reporting these forces are combat-ready and could be expanded to 80,000 personnel if needed. Oil prices surged, with Brent crude reaching $112.10 per barrel, driven by regional tensions and Iran's continued control over the Strait of Hormuz. The US Treasury Department issued a 30-day waiver for Russian oil that is stranded at sea, aimed at ensuring supply stability for "vulnerable countries," a move linked by Press TV to US inability to cope with rising oil prices exacerbated by the Hormuz situation. The Iranian-led Persian Gulf Strait Authority (PGSA) launched an official X account, stating that ships require Iran's approval for passage through the Strait of Hormuz. A powerful explosion was reported near the entrance to the Bab al-Mandeb Strait in the Red Sea.

KEY DEVELOPMENTS
1.  **US Delays Iran Strike:** US President Trump announced the deferment of a planned military strike on Iran, scheduled for May 20, citing requests from Qatar, Saudi Arabia, and the UAE to facilitate ongoing "serious discussions" for an agreement that would prevent Iran from acquiring nuclear weapons.
2.  **Conflicting Negotiation Reports:** The US rejected Iran's latest 14-point proposal, delivered via Pakistan, with a senior US official stating it lacked "meaningful improvement" and warning that "talks will continue through bombs" if Iran does not show flexibility on its nuclear program.
3.  **Iran's Air Defense Activated:** Air defense systems were activated in Isfahan and on Qeshm Island, with Iranian state media reporting interceptions of "enemy drones," identified by Tasnim as US and Israeli unmanned aircraft.
4.  **Flotilla Intercepted:** The Israeli Navy intercepted the "Global Sumud Flotilla," a 57-vessel activist mission from Turkey, attempting to breach the naval blockade on Gaza, arresting activists including six Irish citizens.
5.  **PIJ Commander Killed in Lebanon:** The IDF killed Wael Mahmoud Abd al-Halim, the Palestinian Islamic Jihad commander for Lebanon's Beqaa region, in a precise airstrike near Baalbek; his 17-year-old daughter was also reported killed.
6.  **ICC Warrant for Smotrich:** The International Criminal Court's Office of the Prosecutor in The Hague reportedly filed a request for an international arrest warrant against Israeli Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich for alleged crimes against humanity, war crimes, and apartheid.
7.  **Pakistan Deploys Troops to Saudi Arabia:** Pakistan deployed 8,000 troops, fighter jets (JF-17), drones, and HQ-9 air defense systems to Saudi Arabia as part of a joint defense pact, amid escalating regional tensions.
8.  **San Diego Mosque Shooting:** At least five individuals, including two juvenile attackers and a security guard, were killed in a shooting at an Islamic Center in San Diego, California, with reports indicating "anti-Islamic writings" were found in the attackers' car.

THREAT ASSESSMENT
Escalation risks remain extremely high, primarily between the US and Iran. Despite the temporary halt of a planned US strike, President Trump's statements and those of US officials indicate a rapidly diminishing patience, with warnings that military action could resume "in days, not weeks" or that "talks will continue through bombs." Iran's assertive rhetoric from senior commanders, alongside reported air defense activations against suspected US and Israeli drones, underscore a readiness to retaliate with overwhelming force. The Strait of Hormuz remains a critical flashpoint, with Iran's new PGSA asserting control and escalating oil prices demonstrating its strategic importance.
Active flashpoints include the Israel-Lebanon border, where intense IDF strikes against Hezbollah and PIJ targets are met with Hezbollah rocket and drone attacks. The interception of the Gaza-bound flotilla also creates potential for international diplomatic friction. Military posture changes include the continued presence of US refueling aircraft at Ben Gurion Airport until year-end, signifying sustained US capability in the region, and Pakistan's deployment of significant military assets to Saudi Arabia, bolstering Gulf state defense readiness. Red lines for the US remain clear: Iran must not acquire nuclear weapons, and Trump emphasized no concessions on this. Iran's red lines include demanding full lifting of sanctions and guaranteed sovereign rights in the Strait of Hormuz.

REGIONAL & INTERNATIONAL RESPONSE
**United States:** President Trump halted a planned strike on Iran, citing requests from Qatar, Saudi Arabia, and the UAE, emphasizing that an agreement preventing Iran from acquiring nuclear weapons is paramount. However, US officials expressed dissatisfaction with Iran's latest negotiation proposal, calling it "not sufficient," and warned of potential military action if no significant progress is made. The Pentagon is reportedly preparing for renewed attacks, though it also secretly dismantled a civilian harm prevention program. The US extended a 30-day waiver for Russian oil sanctions to stabilize oil markets. Secretary of State Marco Rubio indicated the "Project Freedom" (escorting ships through Hormuz) was paused at Pakistan's request for diplomatic efforts.
**Gulf States (Saudi Arabia, UAE, Qatar):** These nations directly requested Trump to delay military action against Iran, signaling a preference for diplomatic resolution. Pakistan's deployment of 8,000 troops and military assets to Saudi Arabia under a defense pact underscores the Gulf states' enhanced military posture and concern over regional stability. The UAE's prompt restoration of power at its Barakah nuclear plant after a drone attack highlights vulnerability.
**European Union:** The EU lifted some sanctions against Syrian government entities (Interior and Defense Ministries), for which Syria expressed gratitude. Germany's Foreign Minister Wafdil condemned alleged Iranian drone attacks on the UAE and reiterated that Iran should not achieve nuclear weapons, stressing Europe's need to secure the Strait of Hormuz and Turkey's potential role in ending the conflict. Ireland's President Catherine Connolly expressed pride after her sister was arrested on the Gaza flotilla, demanding international action.
**Russia:** President Putin is visiting China, stating that relations between the two countries are at an unprecedented level, with readiness to support each other's sovereignty. The Kremlin clarified there is no connection between Putin's visit and Trump's (then-planned) strike on Iran.
**China:** Hosts Putin for a visit focused on bilateral relations and cooperation, against the backdrop of an alleged Russian drone strike on a Chinese cargo ship in the Black Sea.
**Turkey:** President Erdogan strongly condemned Israel's interception of the Gaza flotilla as a "new act of piracy" and called for international action to ensure the safe return of its citizens. The Turkish Foreign Minister discussed developments in US-Iran negotiations with his Qatari and Jordanian counterparts.

INTELLIGENCE NOTES
Several contradictions and unverified claims are present in the reporting. Trump's public statements often fluctuate, with him simultaneously announcing a delayed strike due to negotiations and then expressing extreme impatience, stating he is "not open to any concessions," and that Iran knows "what's going to be happening soon." US officials echo this impatience, but details on the "serious discussions" and Iran's "revised proposal" are vague and unconfirmed by multiple sources, leading to a gap in understanding the true state of negotiations.

The claims of US and Israeli drones being intercepted over Qeshm Island by Iranian air defenses come from Tasnim and Iranian officials, which could be an indicator of propaganda to bolster domestic narratives of resilience and deterrence. Similarly, the specific allegations by the IRGC about foiling weapons smuggling from northern Iraq lack independent verification. Press TV's attribution of rising oil prices solely to "Iran's continued control over the Strait of Hormuz" and linking the US Russian oil waiver to inability to cope with these prices is a strong propaganda indicator, oversimplifying complex market dynamics. Omid Dana's channel frequently employs highly inflammatory language ("fuck you," "idiots," "ticking clock," "bomb bomb cutlet") and promotes unverified claims about imminent US ground invasion plans, reflecting a strong pro-monarchist opposition stance and contributing to misinformation.

Reporting gaps include the exact contents of Iran's latest 14-point proposal, the precise nature of the "concessions" the US is or is not willing to make, and concrete evidence supporting claims of US agreement to ease oil sanctions temporarily. The full context and motivation behind the San Diego mosque shooting are not fully clear from the raw feed, beyond the discovery of "anti-Islamic writings." The extent of civilian casualties in Lebanon from Israeli strikes (beyond the PIJ commander's daughter) is also a gap.
